title: Happy Goldston, the drummer, and his stutter
summary: They talk about Goldston's stroke, his funeral parades, and stuttering.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yeah, he lives, is it right up here on the street?
Yeah, that last gate, Arnt Gate there.
Yeah, that's right. We interviewed him about over a year ago. Yeah. Almost two years ago.

I thought he could play music like that. You know, he had a stroke too. Yeah. He was sick for a while, almost gave up, but now he's back and plays on the street again, marches in the... Yeah, marches in the... Yeah, marches in the... Grass band, plays everything.
He sure did. Every time I see him get his drum and see somebody go, he plays the funerals, you know. Yeah, he plays the funerals.
I see him quite often. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, he can stutter. It takes about two minutes to call my name. Sometimes, yeah.

Sometimes he stutters. Yeah, right. Yeah. Other times, though, he doesn't stutter much. Much, yeah. When he talked for us, for Trulaine in the interview, he didn't stutter very much. No, no. No, came right out. Were you there or not?

I believe it's quite natural, you know. I think it's like that, you know, if you're interviewing or anything like that, it looks like you holds up on that, or you call it stut. Right, please. I think that's the way it is. Sometimes, blah, stop there and talk to him sometimes. Plenty of times.
